A_marketable_ioc_fill.setup: Static book (bid 10.00/100, ask 10.02/100). IOC buy limit submitted at ask+$0.01 collar. Run under both exchange models.
A_marketable_ioc_fill.actual_result: FILLED at 10.02, exec_qty=10.0, leaves_qty=0.0 under both -- identical (order size <= touch size, so the two exchange models cannot diverge here)

B_ioc_expiry.actual_result: EXPIRED, exec_qty=0.0, leaves_qty=10.0 under both -- identical

C_queue_trade_depletion_needs_side.setup: Resting GTC buy at bid=10.00 (qty 20 ahead); five TRADE_EVENT prints of qty 10 at 10.00, with vs without a SELL_EVENT bit.
C_queue_trade_depletion_needs_side.actual_result: with_side: FILLED (exec_qty=5.0). without_side: NEW (exec_qty=0.0). Identical under both exchange models.

D_passive_fill_paths.setup: Three probes isolating exactly which fill paths raw L1 data supports for a resting order.
D_passive_fill_paths.d1_trade_through: A trade prints BELOW the resting buy's own price (9.99 vs order at 10.00) -- the unconditional `Ordering::Greater` trade-through arm. with_side: FILLED (exec_qty=5.0). without_side: NEW -- the event never reaches check_if_buy_filled at all without a side bit, not just the queue-depletion arm.
D_passive_fill_paths.d2_depth_zeroed_no_trade: The order's own resting price's quoted qty is driven to 0 with NO trade print at all. Result: NEW in all runs -- on_bid_qty_chg only calls queue_model.depth(), which never calls is_filled() or touches order.status. CORRECTS an earlier version of this fixture/receipt, which incorrectly implied depth going to zero could itself fill a resting order.
D_passive_fill_paths.d3_ask_crosses_down: The opposite quote (best ask) re-quotes down through the resting buy's price (10.02 -> 9.99, order at 10.00). Result: FILLED (exec_qty=5.0) -- via on_best_ask_update, from depth alone, with NO trade data needed at all.

E_optimistic_queue_bias.evidence_class_note: MEASURED, not hand-verified against independently re-derived ProbQueueModel probability math.
E_optimistic_queue_bias.setup: Book only ever quotes 10.00/10.02 until 500ms; a GTC buy is accepted at 9.99 at 50ms while nothing is quoted there (queue.rs new_order() initializes front_q_qty=depth.bid_qty_at_tick(9.99)=0). At 500ms the bid re-quotes to 9.99 showing 50 shares; at 600ms a single 5-share sell-aggressor trade prints at 9.99.
E_optimistic_queue_bias.actual_result: FILLED in full (exec_qty=5.0, exec_price=9.99) on just the 5-share print, despite the level nominally displaying 50 shares -- because the order's internal queue-ahead estimate started at 0 (never having been actually queued behind any real historical volume). This is the optimistic bias the review asked to be documented: an L1-fed backtest can let orders placed away from the touch fill unrealistically fast once the market reaches them, which would skew any fill-rate/time-to-fill/touch-share comparison against a system (like NautilusTrader on the same feed, or a real L3 book) that does not make the same zero-queue-ahead assumption.

evidence.item: Scenario F: NoPartialFillExchange vs PartialFillExchange genuinely diverge
evidence.setup: IOC buy for 150 shares against a touch quoting only 100 shares at 10.02 (collar $0.01, so the order's own limit price is only 1 tick above the touch and no liquidity exists at that further tick either).

actual_result.no_partial_fill: FILLED in full: exec_qty=150.0, exec_price=10.02, leaves_qty=0.0, status=FILLED. NoPartialFillExchange::ack_new's crossing arm (nopartialfillexchange.rs ~330-341) fills the ENTIRE requested quantity unconditionally on any cross, never checking quoted size at all -- documented upstream as 'Regardless of the quantity at the best, liquidity-taking orders will be fully executed at the best... this may cause unrealistic fill simulations if you attempt to execute a large quantity' (doc comment on the struct, ~lines 58-62).
actual_result.partial_fill: EXPIRED, but exec_qty=100.0 (not 0), leaves_qty=50.0. PartialFillExchange::ack_new's IOC arm (partialfillexchange.rs ~437-452) walks quoted depth tick by tick, executes what is actually available (100 shares at the one quoted tick), then -- because the order was not FULLY filled -- overwrites order.status to Expired even though a partial fill already executed and updated position/balance/fee via state.apply_fill(). Reading `order.status` alone therefore UNDERSTATES what happened; exec_qty/leaves_qty must also be read.

evidence.conclusion: The two exchange models are NOT equivalent in general. They coincided on Scenarios A-D and G only because those fixtures kept every order's quantity at or below the touch's quoted size. Any cross-check plan that cares about realistic fill sizing (e.g. large orders relative to displayed size, matching real execution-quality concerns) MUST pick PartialFillExchange deliberately for that reason, not treat the two as interchangeable defaults.
evidence.correction_of: An earlier version of this receipt/README described the two exchange models as producing 'identical' results and used that to imply general equivalence; that was true only for the specific scenarios tested there, and is now corrected.

evidence.item: EMO at-quote rule and Lee-Ready rule, offered separately (previously mislabeled)
evidence.correction: An earlier version of this fixture implemented the rule 'trade at/above ask -> buy; at/below bid -> sell; else tick test' and called it 'Lee-Ready'. That is WRONG: this is the Ellis-Michaely-O'Hara (EMO) 'at-quote' rule (Ellis, Michaely & O'Hara, 2000, Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis, 'The Accuracy of Trade Classification Rules: Evidence from Nasdaq'), which compares to the raw bid/ask quotes. The actual Lee-Ready rule (Lee & Ready, 1991, Journal of Finance, 'Inferring Trade Direction from Intraday Data') compares to the bid-ask MIDPOINT instead. Both rules, and the plain tick test, are compared in the trade-classification literature review at NBER Working Paper No. 14158 (Diether, Lee & Werner, 'Short Sales and Trade Classification Algorithms') -- the citation the review asked for. This fixture now implements and offers BOTH rules separately (infer_side_emo, infer_side_lee_ready), sharing a corrected tick-test fallback (see next item).
evidence.tick_test_fix: The tick-test fallback previously compared only to the IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING trade price, so a run of flat ('zero tick') prints would return an undetermined classification once the immediately preceding price also happened to be identical. It now reuses the LAST KNOWN DIRECTION across any number of consecutive flat ticks (see _tick_test's docstring), which is the standard tick-test definition (compare to the last DIFFERING price).
evidence.coverage_gap_fix: An earlier version of this fixture only fed trades printing exactly at the bid, so the strictly-inside-the-spread tick-test branch never actually executed for either rule. `run_tick_test_coverage_demo()` now runs a 6-print tape (TICK_TEST_TRIGGER_PRICES) specifically designed so: (a) at least one print genuinely falls through the tick test for both rules, (b) a flat-tick run demonstrates direction reuse, and (c) EMO and Lee-Ready are shown to DISAGREE on one print (10.015, strictly inside the spread and above the midpoint after a downtick from 10.02): EMO's tick-test fallback (sensitive to the immediately preceding trade's direction) returns 'sell', while Lee-Ready's direct midpoint rule returns 'buy'. This demonstrates the two rules are not interchangeable, not merely two code paths to the same answer.
evidence.scenario_c_emo_result: Applying the EMO rule to Scenario C's original trade tape (all 5 prints at the bid, 10.00 <= bid 10.00) classifies every one as a sell aggressor -- matching Scenario C's with_side=True case exactly (FILLED, exec_qty=5.0) and restoring trade-driven queue depletion from L1/SIP-shaped data via a data-preparation step external to hftbacktest.
evidence.claim_boundary: This is OUR proposed data-preparation step, explicitly presented as such, not an hftbacktest feature. It is only demonstrated on hand-constructed synthetic tapes, not on real Alpaca SIP data, and its accuracy on real data (where trade-classification error rates for EMO/Lee-Ready are well-documented in the literature to be non-trivial, particularly for NBBO-crossing or off-exchange prints) is not evaluated here.

feasible_for: Order acceptance and marketable-crossing fills driven by top-of-book depth alone (Scenarios A, D3)

IOC/FOK/GTX time-in-force semantics -- crossing IOC/FOK fill at the touch (bundled together under NoPartialFillExchange; FOK is genuinely all-or-none only under PartialFillExchange, see Scenario G); crossing GTX always Expires (never a distinct Rejected status); non-crossing GTX/GTC both rest identically
Constant order latency (entry + response), independent of depth granularity (Scenarios A/B)
TradingValueFeeModel cost accounting on realized fills, verified with a nonzero taker fee (Scenario H)

Both no_partial_fill_exchange and partial_fill_exchange for depth-crossing fill/expiry paths on Scenarios A-D/G's order sizes specifically -- NOT a general equivalence; see 'not_feasible_or_meaningless_for' and Scenario F
not_feasible_or_meaningless_for: Any trade-driven fill path (queue-position depletion via queue_model.trade()/is_filled(), OR the unconditional 'trade-through' arm) without an aggressor side: hftbacktest's exchange models never reach check_if_buy_filled/check_if_sell_filled at all for a side-less TRADE_EVENT, in either exchange model (Scenarios C, D1).

Distinguishing NoPartialFillExchange from PartialFillExchange in general: they diverge sharply once order size exceeds the touch's quoted size (Scenario F) and on FOK-with-insufficient-depth (Scenario G2) -- a cross-check plan MUST pick one deliberately (PartialFillExchange, for realistic fill sizing) rather than treat them as interchangeable.

Trusting a resting order's queue position as realistic when it was accepted at a price the L1 feed had never quoted: queue.rs new_order() seeds queue-ahead from whatever is CURRENTLY quoted there, which is 0 on a fresh L1 price, producing an optimistic fill-speed bias (Scenario E, measured not independently re-derived).
The L3 FIFO queue model, which needs per-order add/cancel/execute events (order_id-level); categorically unavailable from L1 or standard L2 SIP quotes.
Any depth-percentile / multi-level queue heuristic reading levels beyond the touch (our L1 feed only ever has one live level per side).
l1_feasibility_verdict.mitigation: An EMO or Lee-Ready aggressor-side inference step, applied as data preparation before feeding hftbacktest, restores trade-driven queue depletion and trade-through fills in this fixture (see the EMO/Lee-Ready evidence item) -- at the cost of classification error the true exchange-reported side would not have, not quantified here on real data. The queue-position optimism (Scenario E) has no equivalent mitigation identified; it is an inherent property of feeding a queue model data thinner than what it was designed for.
